children: The global gas market could remain tight well into next year as the Iran war chokes off supplies and intensifies competition among importers, and Europe enters the heating season with the lowest levels of gas in storage in more than a decade, the International Energy Agency said in a new report this week.

The IEA forecast the global supply of liquefied natural gas to fall by 3%, or nearly 20 Bcm, this year, as disruptions to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian attacks on key regional infrastructure curbed exports from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.

Non-Persian Gulf LNG production jumped 14% Y/Y, or more than 40 Bcm, between March and October, offsetting two-thirds of the decline in Persian Gulf LNG deliveries, but worldwide LNG production fell by 6% Y/Y, or by ~20 Bcm y-o-y, over the period.

Meanwhile, storage sites across the European Union are entering the 2026-27 heating season with inventories at their lowest levels since 2013, increasing the region's dependence on global LNG supplies to meet winter demand, the IEA said.

Europe's low storage levels could "substantially increase the need for injections to replenish inventories through summer 2027, which could extend global market tightness well into the coming year," the IEA said.

The supply shortfall comes as global gas demand is also expected to weaken this year, declining by ~1.5%, or ~65 Bcm, the IEA said, driven by demand destruction in the Middle East, lower industrial gas consumption in Europe, and a shift from gas to coal in some Asian countries.

title: Global gas market could remain tight well into 2027, IEA warns
